title: Agentic Workflow to Pay Vendors On Time
subtitle: Turning accounts payable from manual data entry into exception management, with AI agents doing the routine work
summary: A task-based accounts payable system for Nuvocargo where AI agents and the AP team share the work of paying carriers on time.

sections.heading: Context
sections.body: As a cross-border freight broker between Mexico and the US, Nuvocargo needed to pay carriers for every completed load. Before issuing each payment, the finance team had to manually collect and approve key documents such as the Proof of Delivery (POD) and the carrier’s invoice.

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: Carrier payments were consistently delayed, which hurt our credit score and reputation with carriers. As a result, carriers charged us higher rates, lowering the brokerage’s margins.

sections.heading: Process
sections.body:
We started by sitting with the Finance and Carrier Ops teams to understand the root causes of the delayed payments:
- The Proof of Delivery went through multiple handoffs across different departments on the carrier’s side.
- Once our team received the documents, they had to manually verify that the data matched our system.
- Rejection reasons weren’t clear, and there was no tool for the team to follow up on pending documents.

Next, we built the foundational pieces the agentic workflow needed, such as automated document validation and line item statuses for the Purchase Order.

Lastly, we defined the criteria for a Purchase Order to be executed in the TMS, which triggered the payment in TriumphPay:
- POD approved
- Invoice approved
- All payable line items approved

images.alt: Whiteboard mapping the carrier invoice and payment workflow, including approval scenarios and statuses

sections.heading: Solution
sections.body:
We built an agentic workflow that started the moment a shipment arrived at its destination, and took care of the repetitive tasks in three steps:
- Collection: The agent reached out to the driver via SMS to request the POD. If it couldn’t get it, it reached out to the dispatcher, and later requested the invoice from the billing department.
- Validation: Once the documents were in the system, the agent checked that their data matched our records. When the invoice total didn’t match, the agent created a line item for the difference with a “Review” status, so a rep could find where it came from and decide whether to approve or reject it.
- Execution: Once the POD, the invoice and all payable line items were approved, the purchase order was executed automatically and payment was issued through the ERP.

If a document couldn’t be collected or validated within the expected time, the agent created an escalation with all the context needed for a human to step in and take the right action.

images.alt: NuvoOS shipments table with POD and invoice statuses, a shipment’s financials tab where the Pay Vendor agentic workflow flags an invoice mismatch, and the workflow’s completed conditions: POD approved, invoice approved, payment issued via TriumphPay

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: Time to pay carriers decreased by 55%, and purchase orders that met all criteria were executed and paid without anyone touching them. Finance and Carrier Ops only stepped in when the agent raised an escalation, shifting their role from manual data entry and follow-ups to incident management. Paying carriers stopped taking up more bandwidth with every new load and became a scalable workflow that also improved Nuvocargo’s credit score and reputation with carriers.

title: System Design to Invoice Customers and Improve Cash Flow
subtitle: Redesigning how invoices and financial data come together so the team can bill customers faster
summary: A redesign of Nuvocargo’s Financials Tab and accounts receivable workflow, built to get invoices out faster and improve cash flow.

sections.heading: Context
sections.body: A load could only be invoiced to a customer once it met certain criteria, such as being delivered to its destination and having a complete set of documents.

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body:
A common challenge in freight brokerage is a cash flow shortage. Brokers must pay carriers shortly after a shipment is delivered, while shippers can take 30 to 60 days to pay their invoices. Every day an invoice goes out late widens that gap.

At Nuvocargo, the finance team lacked a tool that showed which delivered loads were ready to be invoiced and which were still missing documentation.

Additionally, the experience wasn’t built for finance reps to quickly create invoices from within their workflow. It required going back and forth between interfaces.

sections.heading: Process
sections.body:
We started by understanding how the team was operating. Their tools were scattered, and some of the data was inconsistent. People on the same team worked with different tools, such as data dashboards and spreadsheets, because NuvoOS wasn’t giving them the visibility they needed.

From there, we defined the stages a load goes through before it’s ready to invoice.

sections.heading: Solution
sections.body:
We redesigned the data tables with clearer stages and visibility into which invoicing requirements were met. We added new statuses and filters, reorganized the columns, and added a side panel for each Sales Order so reps could review and execute it quickly. For loads with defects, the team could see what was missing and who in the operation to follow up with.

I owned the end-to-end execution and deployment of this project using Piloto, our internal coding platform.

images.alt: NuvoOS Receivables table with Ready To Invoice view, POD and line item statuses, next to a Sales Order side panel with documents, revenue line items, order summary, and an Execute button

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: Gave the finance team clear visibility into which loads were ready to invoice and made it easier to execute them, reducing the time to invoice customers and improving cash flow.

testimonials.quote: Thanks for the constant push you make with the operation to make the project succeed. I know working with the ops team can be really difficult, however sometimes we need a push from someone like you to make things happen. You were on top of the project since day one.

sections.heading: Vision
sections.body: This was the foundational phase of a larger effort to automate Sales Order execution once all the criteria were met, the same way we did for carrier Purchase Orders. At the time, customers had a wide range of invoicing preferences that our system hadn’t standardized yet, so standardizing them was the next step toward automation.

title: Prototyping and Deployment of a Customer-Facing Platform
subtitle: Prototyping the Control Tower in code to give 4PL shippers visibility and insights into their freight
summary: Designing the front end of Nuvocargo’s Control Tower, the customer-facing platform for 4PL shippers, and prototyping it in code.

sections.heading: Context
sections.body: Nuvocargo’s 4PL (Fourth Party Logistics) customers had access to the Control Tower, an external-facing platform that surfaced data from the TMS so customers could see the status of their freight.

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: As the growth strategy shifted toward 4PL accounts, the Control Tower became a key resource for attracting new customers and increasing the satisfaction of existing ones.

sections.heading: Process
sections.body:
I began the redesign by conducting research with internal stakeholders and with people at different levels on the customers’ side. This helped me understand what shippers in this segment valued most from their logistics providers:
- Visibility into their loads and daily operations
- Insights into their service performance and freight spend

sections.heading: Solution
sections.body:
I used our tech stack and agentic coding to prototype the new front end of the Control Tower. The redesign gave shippers clear visibility into their active loads, with a new drawer component to preview each load’s details. They could also see historical data for each lane, with AI-generated insights to help them improve service performance and optimize freight spend.

On this project I partnered with members of the C-suite. My output was a code branch with every design decision built in, using AI to eliminate the design-to-engineering handoff.

images.alt: Control Tower overview: a map of active shipments with filters for All Shipments, Need Attention, Picking Up Today, and Delivering Today, and a drawer showing a shipment’s pickup, delivery, and tracking milestones
Cost and Service Performance dashboard with volume, average cost per pound, on-time delivery, and tender acceptance, above a map of the shipper’s supply chain network
AI-generated insights powered by NuvoAI showing how much spend the shipper can recover and how much on-time delivery can improve, above a table of cost and service performance by delivery location
Lane detail for Dallas, TX to Houston, TX with a route map, lane metrics, and AI prompts for saving money and improving service on the lane

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The redesign drove higher engagement from existing customers and generated interest from prospects.

title: UI Design for Agentic Appointment Scheduling
subtitle: Designing how people follow AI agents as they schedule pickups and deliveries, and step in when something goes wrong
summary: New design system components that show the progress of the agentic workflow for appointment scheduling at Nuvocargo, and make escalations clear and actionable.

sections.heading: Context
sections.body: Every shipment has a pickup and a delivery, and sometimes more than one of each. Every stop needs a scheduled appointment. We automated appointment scheduling with AI agents that emailed, called, or logged into facility portals to confirm when a shipment could be picked up or dropped off.

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: As we started implementing agentic workflows across the freight brokerage lifecycle, we needed a new way to display those automations so users could easily follow their progress. When an AI agent escalated a workflow, users needed clarity on what the issue was and what action they could take to solve it.

sections.heading: Process
sections.body: I partnered with the engineering team building this automation to understand the different use cases and the ways appointments could be scheduled at pickup and delivery locations.

sections.heading: Solution
sections.body: I used our design system to create new components that displayed the progress of these workflows, and the information around them, in a clear, actionable way. Users could see when an AI agent was already working on an appointment, or when there was an issue that needed to be solved. For escalations, the stop showed the facility’s contact details so the user could resolve it right away.

images.alt: Appointment scheduling flow: from a shipment’s stops, users request an appointment from the Scheduling Agent or set one manually by email or facility portal; the stop then shows the agent’s progress, and escalates to human review with the facility’s contact details when needed

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: Customer Ops no longer needed to contact facilities to schedule appointments, and only stepped in when human input was needed.

title: Scope and Design of an End-to-End Solution for Enterprise Customers
subtitle: Extending the TMS to support multi-stop shipments so Nuvocargo could sign its first 4PL enterprise customer
summary: Scoping and designing the changes across the freight lifecycle that let Nuvocargo’s TMS support enterprise shippers and their multi-stop shipments.

sections.heading: Context
sections.body: In 2024, we were working to sign our first 4PL enterprise customer. These shippers operated differently from the customers our TMS was originally built for.

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: The first version of our TMS didn’t fully support the way enterprise customers operated. To sign our first multi-million-dollar contract, our product needed to handle how they worked.

sections.heading: Process
sections.body:
We dove deep into their end-to-end operation to understand what fell outside our standard flow.

One of the main differences was that these shippers serviced their own customers, delivering goods to different customers’ warehouses in a single shipment. In other words, multi-stop shipments.

sections.heading: Solution
sections.body: The different stops of a shipment needed to be accounted for during quoting, pricing, appointment scheduling, tracking, and invoicing. We scoped and designed every adjustment the v1 workflow needed to handle this operation across the entire freight lifecycle.

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: We signed our first 4PL enterprise customer, a multi-million-dollar contract.
